source.title: Psychobiological mechanisms underlying the social buffering of the hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenocortical axis: a review of animal models and human studies across development

confidence_rationale: Authoritative cross-species, cross-development review establishing social buffering -- a dampened HPA-axis stress response in the presence/assistance of a conspecific -- as a distinct psychobiological process mediated by oxytocinergic systems and prefrontal networks, shaped by early experience. Supports the differentiation verdict's central claim that SOOTHING/COMFORT is a mechanistically separate system from relief (reward-circuit offset) and safety (cortico-amygdalar prediction): it operates on the ONGOING neuroendocrine/autonomic stress state via an external (social) regulator, not as event reinforcement or prospective threat-absence prediction. claim_ids_tested intentionally empty -- REE has no registered soothing/social-buffering mechanism; this entry grounds a PROPOSED extension-register row, not an existing claim. Source quality high (Psychological Bulletin integrative review); mapping fidelity to REE moderate-low (REE V3 lacks a conspecific/other-model, so the canonical social trigger is V4); transfer risk moderate-high.
failure_signatures: Social buffering is gated by a CONSPECIFIC's presence/assistance -- REE V3 has no other-model, so the canonical trigger cannot be instantiated until V4-social; building soothing in V3 by emotion-name would be premature.

The mediators are oxytocinergic + prefrontal + developmentally-shaped attachment, not the value-coding dopamine of relief nor the conditioned-inhibition prediction of safety -- folding soothing into MECH-302 (relief) or MECH-303/304 (safety) would mis-assign the substrate.
Early-experience dependence: buffering capacity is shaped by developmental attachment history -- a state REE has no representation of.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Social buffering is a cross-species process consisting of a dampened HPA-axis stress response to threat/challenge in the presence or with the assistance of a conspecific; its putative mediators are oxytocinergic systems and prefrontal neural networks, and early experience is critical in shaping later social buffering effects.
mapping.ree_translation: Proposed SOOTHING/COMFORT affect stream (NOT yet registered): an autonomic/neuroendocrine down-regulation of the ONGOING stress/drive state, externally (socially) triggered, that reduces the magnitude and recovery time of the active suffering/drive trajectory. In REE terms it would act as a state-GAIN/recovery modulator on the suffering accumulator (MECH-219) and homeostatic drive (SD-012, SD-032e pACC autonomic coupling) -- distinct from relief's offset reinforcement (MECH-302) and safety's prospective prediction (MECH-303/304).
mapping.mapping_caveat: The canonical mechanism requires a conspecific (social buffering), which REE V3 cannot represent (no other-model) -- this is the basis for the V4-social scope recommendation. A non-social autonomic-recovery core (parasympathetic down-regulation of ongoing arousal) could in principle be a minimal V3 hook, but that is an extrapolation beyond what this social-buffering review tests. claim_ids_tested is empty because no soothing mechanism is registered; this entry is forward-looking grounding for the extension-register decision.
mapping.source_context: Integrative review across rodent models and human studies, infancy to adulthood; HPA-axis cortisol/corticosterone outcomes; oxytocin and prefrontal mediation.

confidence_components.notes: High-quality canonical review; the differentiation verdict it supports is strong, but REE-mapping fidelity is held down by the absence of any V3 other-model and the developmental-attachment dependence. Net 0.78 for 'soothing is a distinct system'; lower if read as direct REE-implementation evidence.
